invariants.area: erasure clocks, cutoffs, and worker failure
invariants.trace: The lane reservation and molecule guards still precede cutoff checks and enqueue. Cutoff comparisons, missing-target policies, and author-clock assignment remain unchanged. The lane still waits for the author clock before dispatch. Terminal results still enter pending_completion and reach the sender only after lane byte release. Retry and quarantine behavior remain unchanged. PurgeEnvelope retains optional completion fields because preparation and inline peer deletion create jobs without a channel, and the release step takes each sender once. Mixed batches retain their explicit native flush, including the all-spared case.

The logical guard rejects standalone ranges and patterns. HashKey, HashRangeKey, HashRangeKeys, HashRangePrefix, and HashRangeRange retain the caller hash in their narrowed producers; exact and batch reads retain supplied ranges, and collect_matches decodes OPE ranges. Warm exact reads construct API CorePaths. These five selectors therefore bypass value-based hash recovery. None, Page, PageAfter, and SampleN retain physical key recovery and opaque-key accounting. The removed one-dimensional Hash scan arm had no caller: both former call sites supplied the Range slot.

Count gathers the already resolved API keys from the same field readers. The removed second hash transformation could mistake a distinct valid API hash for an encoded twin. The HashSet still removes identical logical keys. Named-spine authority, one selected fallback field, namespace union, tombstone checks, and named-layout value checks remain unchanged. The count caller contract excludes physical page bounds.

Timeout now produces ReadResourceLimit. Key-budget errors already use that typed error, StorageError conversion preserves typed limits, and generation-pointer reads now preserve read/write limits. fail_key_load selects DiskOnly for those types and Failed for other errors. Both outcomes detach the partial domain, clear pending deltas, preserve the error reason, and notify waiters. This removes wording-dependent fallback without admitting incomplete keys.

PreparedCommit owns SpaceReservation directly. Replacement space is acquired before the earlier prepared owner drops. Success releases the charge at the former release_space point. Journal failure moves it to failed_write; subsequent admission refuses a failed writer, so the new lifetime comment correctly states retention until runtime drop. Both queue failure branches leave the sealed requests vector intact. Only complete success clears that vector; removal of failed_requests does not remove PendingBatch ownership.
